{"draft": "Second-Quarter Profit Climbs on Higher Revenue and Airfreight Tonnage

Expeditors International reported higher second-quarter results, with revenue and profit advancing as airfreight volumes strengthened. Revenues rose 32% to $3.5 billion, operating income climbed 41% to $350 million, and net earnings attributable to shareholders grew 45% to $266 million. Diluted net earnings attributable to shareholders per share jumped 51% to $2.03.

Airfreight tonnage increased 14% from a year earlier, while ocean container volume remained flat. Tonnage also rose 16% compared with the first quarter of 2026, helped by trade lanes including Asia-U.S. and Asia-Europe. Volumes advanced 7% compared with the first quarter of 2026.

The companys results included a $25 million pretax restructuring charge related to its Global Technology team. Expeditors said the restructuring is expected to lower its cost structure by approximately $50 million annually, equating to nearly 10% of total corporate overhead expenses. The charge was partly offset by a $16 million gain on the sale of an underutilized property during the quarter.

Operating efficiency improved to 32.2% in the second quarter, inclusive of the restructuring charge. The company said second-quarter headcount remained essentially flat versus the first quarter of 2026, with reductions tied to the restructuring mainly expected to be realized in the third quarter.

Expeditors returned $461 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases during the second quarter, bringing the total for the first half of 2026 to $748 million. During the three months ended June 30, 2026, the company repurchased 2.3 million shares at an average price of $151.50.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Expeditors repurchased 4.3 million shares at an average price of $148.87. The company also plans an Investor Day in New York City in November 2026 for shareholders and analysts."}
